effect: Sovereign ratings respond to a country's own economy the way agencies do. The game's rating is one regression fitted across countries (fast-growing emerging economies rate worse), applied within one country over time, so a boom worsened the rating, inflation was nearly free, and debt moved it only 0.0135 notch per point. The cross-country fit stays as the level; from a reference taken on day 365 (the first year runs as in the original, because day-0 growth is partly seeded from observed data and decays during it), changes against the reference use within-country weights: growth -0.15 notch per point above the reference (a boom improves the rating, a recession of 5 points below costs about 0.75 notch), inflation +0.05 notch per point above it plus a further +0.1 per point above 10 on the game's log inflation scale (about 10.5% inflation; sustained double-digit inflation costs several notches, as Turkey and Argentina saw), and debt above a threshold +1 notch per 20 points of GDP (relative to the excess at the reference, so countries already above the threshold do not start worse). The threshold is 90% of GDP for issuers of a reserve currency and for currency-union members (agencies tolerate more debt there, e.g. Japan) and 60% for every other country (emerging markets are downgraded from about 50-60%). The cross-country growth and inflation weights no longer move a country's own rating after the reference. The threshold is fixed when the reference is taken, so a currency gaining or losing reserve status later (the game flips it on inflation streaks) does not jump the rating. The reference (growth, inflation, debt ratio, threshold) is stored on the country (geobalRatingRef) by the rating tick; a reference saved by mod 0.1.0 (which stored only the excess above 90%) is completed on the first rating tick with the reference debt that reproduces 0.1.0's debt term exactly at that moment (T + max(0, debt - T) - max(0, debt - 90) + excess, T the country's threshold), so loading such a save does not move the rating. The debt-crisis test (P7) drops its cliff at debt above 170% of GDP with a rating of 16 or worse: high debt now works through the rating slope, and the crisis paths still open at rating 18 or debt above 400% (no country is under the dropped clause at day 0). A defaulted country rates D (19) only while restructured debt is still owed (the game's rule since build 26346311); no reference is taken while it rates D, and one is taken on the first rating tick after it repays. Day 0 unchanged: none of the within-country terms (growth, inflation, the 60%/90% debt thresholds) act before the day-365 reference, and no country is under the dropped crisis clause at day 0. The rating breakdown shown in the UI still lists the original terms. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26296134; the patch's find text has the current ones.)
